applies_why: The judge text resolves D5 vs C5 by saying CR2 G answers the almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows but the sign's sense remains open, so it is judging the pressing chain/link by the openness of Isaiah 7:14 rather than by chain-against-chain footing.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' — I weighed whether 'leaving the sign's sense open' is a chain-by-footing conclusion or an open-verse/verse-by-verse reason.
why: The stated reason lets the open sense of the sign control the matchup instead of requiring the pressed chain to be weighed against the link by footing, which is what K-C forbids.
